jobs.prompt: TOP PRIORITY, root cause of the endless the checkout has uncommitted changes blockers (atlas-seafloor, and every project): swarm rewrites generated state files after nearly every command (coordination/HANDOFF.md, docs/scope/build-plan.md, docs/state/usage-ledger.md and a few more), so the working tree is always dirty and every finished run blocks the next integrate, merge or autopilot step. Fix: generated state files never count as a dirty tree, and they are not rewritten when nothing but a timestamp changed. PART 1, one shared classifier: new module tools/generated-state.mjs exporting GENERATED_STATE (the list of repo-relative paths and prefixes) and isGeneratedStateFile(relPath) and filterGeneratedStatus(lines) and dirtyFiles(root, { exec, untracked = true }) (runs git status --porcelain=v1 -z with an explicit argument array, parses it exactly, drops generated state files, returns the remaining list with their status codes; paths are normalized and compared case-sensitively; a path with .. or an absolute path is never generated state). The generated state list: coordination/HANDOFF.md, coordination/HANDOFF.previous.md, coordination/HANDOFF.previous-2.md, coordination/TASK.md, docs/scope/build-plan.md, docs/scope/context/ (every file under it, written by scope approve), docs/scope/waves/ (every file under it), docs/state/usage-ledger.md, and everything under .swarm/. NOT generated state: docs/scope/roadmap.md or any scope source file, docs/plans/, source, tests, manifests (coordination/manifests/), package files, workflows. Use it in EVERY clean-checkout test and nowhere else: find each place that refuses or decides because the checkout is dirty and replace its status call with dirtyFiles (or filterGeneratedStatus): tools/autopilot.mjs checkout.dirty (line ~380) and the worktreeDirty function in tools/swarm.mjs it is fed from (lines ~2332 and ~3829 to ~3840), tools/goal.mjs (the dirty dependency at lines ~64 and ~155, message goal-dirty), tools/merge-guard.mjs (line ~121, swarm merge), tools/pipeline.mjs (line ~91), tools/ship.mjs (the two status calls at ~1070 and ~1665, keeping their existing untracked setting and their existing ignore of generated files if any: unify on the shared list), and clean-branch-dirty in tools/swarm/core-12.mjs (line ~44). Read each call site first; do NOT change checks that are about something else (the gitDirty(dir, [tools, skills]) check in install and update stays as it is, the dirty status of a job worktree in tools/swarm/workspace.mjs stays, spend.mjs stays). The messages stay the same but list the first 5 offending files so the owner sees what is dirty (never the generated ones). PART 2, HANDOFF.md regenerates correctly and includes pending approvals from the worktrees. Find the code that writes coordination/HANDOFF.md (search the tools folder for HANDOFF.md; likely tools/orchestrator-context.mjs, tools/project-commands.mjs and the writer in the tools/swarm folder; reuse, do not duplicate). Requirements: (a) the content is generated from live state every time (never appended to or merged with stale text); the rotation to HANDOFF.previous.md and HANDOFF.previous-2.md only happens when the content really changed; (b) the file is NOT rewritten when the new content equals the old content apart from the generated-at timestamp line(s) (compare with the timestamp lines masked): no write, no rotation, so the tree is not touched by read-only commands; (c) writes are atomic (temp file in the same folder plus rename); (d) it includes a section Pending approvals that lists every open owner item for the project AND for every linked worktree of the same repository (git worktree list --porcelain, run with an argument array; read each worktree path's own state: open hand-build requests, owner decisions, policy requests, change orders, tickets waiting on the owner, merge approvals), each line showing the kind, the id, the age, the branch and the worktree path (the main checkout is labelled main checkout); worktrees of the repository are included even when they live under the scratch base (they are this project's own); a missing or unreadable worktree is listed as unreadable, never aborts the generation; entries are sorted (newest first, then id) so output is stable; (e) the section says none when there is nothing pending. Keep every existing HANDOFF test passing and the HANDOFF format otherwise unchanged. Tests in tests/generated-state.test.mjs and tests/handoff-regenerate.test.mjs, hermetic (temp git repos and worktrees, git with explicit config, explicit environment, no ambient environment, injected clock): isGeneratedStateFile truth table (every listed path and prefix, near misses such as docs/scope/roadmap.md, docs/plans/ideas.md, coordination/manifests/x.json, a path with .., an absolute path, case variants); dirtyFiles with only generated files modified, added, deleted, renamed and untracked returns empty; with one source file dirty returns just that file; each call site: the autopilot checkout check, goal, merge-guard, pipeline, ship and clean-branch pass with only generated state dirty and still block with another dirty file (and list it); a read-only command after HANDOFF exists does not modify the file (mtime and bytes), a changed state rewrites it and rotates once, a timestamp-only difference writes nothing; the Pending approvals section lists a hand-build request filed in a linked worktree with its branch and path, lists a main-checkout item, says none when empty, survives an unreadable worktree, is sorted stably; the write is atomic (no partial file when the write fails). Keep every existing test passing (autopilot, goal, merge-guard, pipeline, ship, handoff, completion). No token-shaped literals. ignoreTests reason: tests that reference swarm.mjs and these files in passing are covered by the full suite run before merge.
